extracted.intended_audience: business personnel and EHS/compliance professionals working with Japanese environmental regulations
extracted.subtask_short: overview of Japanese laws and regulations
extracted.subtask_description: A concise explanatory overview of the hierarchy, meanings, and issuance authorities of legal instruments in Japan, with emphasis on items relevant to environmental regulation and business compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the term 'laws and regulations' (法令)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different authorities define 'laws and regulations' variously; National Diet Library includes the constitution, treaties, laws, cabinet orders, ministerial orders, public notifications, regulations, agency orders, directives, and notices, while the government e-GOV site lists the constitution, laws, cabinet orders, imperial orders, cabinet office orders, ministerial orders, and regulations and treats instructions/circular notices/prescribed forms separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that 'laws and regulations' is interpreted differently across sources and is not fixed by the Constitution. For business legal compliance, explicitly distinguish among the different document types (laws, cabinet orders, ministerial orders, public notifications, circular notices, communications) rather than relying on a single broad definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws (法律 / ho-ritsu)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws are enacted by passage of bills by both Houses of the Diet, or by the House of Representatives under its legislative supremacy. From the perspective of business activity, laws have the highest priority among all laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat statutory law as supreme for compliance matters (many constitutional provisions require actions to be 'determined by law'); regulatory measures must be traced to enabling statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cabinet orders (政令 / sei-rei)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Constitution (Article 73) mandates the Cabinet to 'enact cabinet orders in order to execute the provisions of this Constitution and of the law.' Cabinet orders generally cannot include penal provisions unless authorized by law. Enforcement orders, intended to enforce a relevant law, are issued as cabinet orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize cabinet orders as executive-level instruments used to implement statutes; check statutory authorization before treating any cabinet order as imposing penalties. For environmental rules, enforcement orders may be issued as cabinet orders and should be consulted when interpreting statutory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial orders (省令 / sho-rei)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the National Government Organization Act (Article 12), a minister may issue a Ministerial Ordinance to enforce an Act or a Cabinet Order concerning administrative matters under the minister's charge, or under a special delegation. Ministerial orders may not include penal provisions unless authorized by law. Enforcement regulations are issued as ministerial orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministerial orders are the ministry-level implementing regulations. For compliance, identify relevant ministerial ordinances and enforcement regulations that operationalize statutory or cabinet-order requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of enforcement orders and enforcement regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement orders are issued as cabinet orders; enforcement regulations are issued as ministerial orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking the concrete rules that operationalize a statute, check both cabinet-level enforcement orders and ministry-level enforcement regulations, and note which instrument is authorized by the enabling statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notifications (告示 / koku-ji)
rubrics_metrics.description: National Government Organization Act Article 14.1 provides that a minister, a commission or the director-general of an agency may issue a public notification in respect of affairs under their jurisdiction when it is necessary to issue a public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notifications are formal notices issued by ministries/agencies to inform the public of matters within their jurisdiction; they can be relevant to compliance when they announce application rules, effective dates, or lists required by law/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circular notices / instructions (通達 / tsu-tatsu)
rubrics_metrics.description: National Government Organization Act Article 14.2 provides that a minister, a commission or the director-general of an agency may issue an instruction or a circular notice to competent organs and officials for the purpose of giving an order or direction regarding affairs under their jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circular notices are generally internal administrative directions aimed at subordinate organs and officials; while influential in enforcement practice, they may not have the same legal force as laws or orders and should be treated as guidance for administrative implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications (通知 / tsu-chi) and subordinate notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications (通知) are generally issued by heads of subordinate organizations (e.g., director-general of a Bureau) rather than by heads of ministries. They are used to publicly inform and, in practice, may resemble public notifications (告示) since they can require public notification; examples include communications by director-generals or joint notifications across bureaus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider communications as additional administrative instruments that can affect compliance expectations; check whether a 'communication' is intended as internal guidance or as a public-facing notice with practical legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy and practical priority among legal instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Although definitions vary, there is a practical hierarchy: Constitution at the top, followed by laws (statutes), then cabinet orders, ministerial orders, public notifications, circular notices, and other administrative documents. The page emphasizes that for business compliance one should distinguish among these categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In compliance workflows, map requirements back to their source instrument and authority (statute, cabinet order, ministerial order); prioritize statutory obligations and verify whether subordinate instruments are authorized by enabling statutes before treating them as binding.
